Now let's look at the first tricky situation — **when the automatic detail-gathering fails** (an unreachable page, a dead link, no network). I've made the prototype simulate that for any link on an unreachable host. Refresh **http://maker:4001**.

> **1.** In the save box, paste `https://broken.example.com/gone` and press **Save**.
> **2.** After the brief attempt, the bookmark is **still saved** — nothing is lost — but shows a gentle warning that the page's details couldn't be fetched. The link itself stands in as the title.
> **3.** You get a **Try again** action (in case it was a temporary hiccup) and the normal **Edit** so you can fill in the title/description yourself.

The thinking behind this: since your real goal is never losing a link, a failed fetch should never block saving — it saves anyway and lets you recover.

Does that handling feel right — **save the link regardless, warn, and let me retry or fill it in myself**? Or would you rather a failed fetch behave differently (for example, refuse to save until it succeeds)?
